candidates.title: Kate
candidates.reason: Strong whole-film action evidence: Odie Henderson's 106-minute review calls the violence wall-to-wall carnage, while The Harvard Crimson describes a bloody, action-packed film with distinct restaurant, kitchen-weapon and street shoot-out fights. The Playlist independently describes recurring gunfights, car chases and hand-to-hand combat across neon-lit Tokyo, supporting high action density as distinct from the force of its peak set pieces. The poisoned assassin's less-than-24-hour revenge pursuit supplies an urgent high-concept hook, capable lead and evolving uneasy partnership with Ani. Limitations: critics disagree on entertainment value, with RogerEbert.com calling the violence monotonous and the plot derivative; other reviews note predictable twists, a choppy setup and intermittent emotional scenes. Gunplay and melee are more strongly established than destruction or fantasy; visual variety is primarily urban nightlife, not an assumption of many different regions.

research_rejections.title: The Princess
research_rejections.reason: Although the 94-minute castle escape contains repeated sword and hand-to-hand fights, RogerEbert.com's whole-film review reports flashback interruptions and a stop-start pattern, while other reviews criticize repeated encounters in a confined castle and weak presentation. Its action is not assumed to be absent, but sustained density and sufficient variation are less secure than for the shortlisted film; withheld from this research packet rather than inventing a strong fit.
